Actual Article Body:
A project of
			Freedom of the Press Foundation

President Donald Trump boarding Air Force One on Oct. 21, 2026, at Joint Base Andrews, Maryland. That day, his administration informed reporter Andrew Feinberg of The Independent he would be barred from traveling on the aircraft the next day.

The Independent’s reporter Andrew Feinberg was blocked from serving as the in-town press pooler by the White House on Nov. 6, 2026, the second time in two weeks he has been barred from covering the president.

Feinberg was previously booted from serving as the travel print press pooler for an Air Force One trip Oct. 22, after President Donald Trump berated him in a tense exchange in the Oval Office two days before.

News of The Independent’s latest access denial was first reported by CNN’s Brian Stelter, who also said that the White House had selected as Feinberg’s replacement Daniel Baldwin of One America News Network, characterized by media analysts as a right-leaning outlet friendly to the president.

Feinberg confirmed to the U.S. Press Freedom Tracker that he was the target of the block, but declined to comment further for this story.

The Independent’s White House correspondent Andrew Feinberg learned on Oct. 21, 2026, that he would be excluded from traveling with President Donald Trump aboard Air Force One the following day for a planned trip.

Feinberg was scheduled to join the traveling press pool accompanying the president to a campaign rally in Iowa on Oct. 22. However, White House communications staff removed him from the approved list of travelers on the eve of the trip, the British news outlet reported.

The move followed a contentious exchange between the reporter and the president in the Oval Office on Oct. 20. After Feinberg asked Trump a question about the construction of a golf course in Washington, D.C., the president told him to be quiet and said, “What’s wrong with you? Are you a sick person?”

The White House’s Rapid Response X account later referred to Feinberg with a slur for a person with Down syndrome, while Vice President JD Vance referred to the reporter with a similarly offensive term on his social media.

The administration has in recent weeks booted reporters, including from CNN and Politico, off Air Force One flights amid a high-profile legal battle over whether the president can unilaterally ban outlets from the White House complex.
